title: Tracing Inputs, Verifying Outputs: Validating Attribution in Music Generation
subtitle: Audio examples for an anonymous submission under review at ICLR 2027.
overview_html:
Euterpe generates any number of stems of any instrument. Its only input is registered audio, and we argue that tracing that audio is enough for attribution: knowing who should be paid. For this the model must meet two requirements:

  1. Its output follows the input audio closely.
  2. It reproduces training data only to a negligible degree.

We validate the model on these two points. Below are the audio examples used in the validation.
footer_html: Anonymous submission. This page loads no external resources.

sections.title: Any-Stem Generation
sections.intro_html: The prompt shapes the timbre and playing style of the generated stem, the context its rhythm and harmony, so prompt use maps to recording rights and context use to publishing (composition) rights.

sections.title: Memorization Audit
sections.intro_html: Does the model reproduce a training stem? Unlike previous audits, the main retrievers are version-matching models insensitive to timbre (Argus, CLEWS; CLAP and MERT for comparison): each generated stem is the query, its nearest training stem in the embedding space is retrieved, and the pair is judged by listening. Here are the top-ranked generated stems next to the training stems they retrieved.

floats.label: Figure 2
floats.title: Verdict Procedure for the Memorization Audit
floats.caption: Figure 2 of the paper. The verdict procedure of the memorization audit, read top to bottom. Orange: Type I and II, the uncovered memorizations; blue: other memorization. Badges: counts for the Argus validation band.
